title: Bear persecution patiently, forgive, and renounce war
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation in Kirtland, Ohio, on 6 August 1833. Two weeks earlier, a mob in Independence, Missouri, had destroyed the Church printing office and tarred and feathered Bishop Edward Partridge and Charles Allen. On 23 July, Church leaders there agreed under pressure to leave Jackson County. The official heading says Joseph could have known the seriousness of events only by revelation. The Joseph Smith Papers notes the text never names Jackson County and may also reflect rising opposition in Kirtland. It was copied into a letter to Missouri the same day.
summary: The revelation tells the Saints not to fear, to give thanks, and to wait on the Lord. It promises that their afflictions will work together for their good. It says the constitutional law that protects freedom is justified, and that honest and wise leaders should be sought. It calls the Saints to renounce war and proclaim peace. It rebukes many in the Kirtland church for pride and covetousness. Then it gives a law for enduring attacks: bear the first, second, and third offense patiently. After warning an enemy, the injured may be justified in defending themselves. It also gives an ancient pattern of offering peace three times before war, It commands forgiveness of a repentant enemy every time. An unrepentant enemy is forgiven three times, and the fourth offense is brought before the Lord.

contextNote.title: Peace offered before any defense
contextNote.text: The Saints faced violence and had to decide how to respond. Verse 16 sets the main direction, telling them to “renounce war and proclaim peace”. Verses 23–27 explain what that means under attack. Each offense borne patiently brings a greater reward and stands as a testimony against the attacker. Verses 33–36 give the same pattern for nations: lift a standard of peace three times before any battle. Verses 39–40 add that a repentant enemy must always be forgiven. In this passage, renouncing war means exhausting peace first, not merely avoiding fights.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson “Be Still and Know That I Am God” covers sections 98–101. It teaches that the Lord asks His people to seek peace and to trust that afflictions can work for their good. How do verses 23–27 and 39–40 describe the way to respond when someone wrongs you repeatedly?
reviewNote: Read all 48 verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, 6 August 1833, in response to the Missouri persecution, and says Joseph could have known the situation only by revelation. JSP historical introduction says Joseph apparently did not know of the specific July events, that the text does not name Jackson County, and that it may relate to tensions in Kirtland (the Hurlbut affair) as well. Both framings are noted in the setting. Partridge is named in the setting only. Fact-check 2026-10-12: summary omitted verses 41–45 (forgiving an unrepentant enemy three times, then bringing testimonies before the Lord). Added. Fact-check 2026-10-12: contextNote added “in every setting” to verse 16, which the text does not say. Removed.
